visualReview.notes: Inspected the low lake-side curtain and higher roofed towers, stone opening recesses, rounded battery and lookout, distinct courtyard levels, and landward timber leaf and bridge rails.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Inspected all four sides, overhead, and the lake front, battery, terraced court, and bridge closeups. The raised window and roof details and stone coping read in the shared surfaces. The mapped placement unload passed.

mediumFiReview.notes: Inspected all 25 water-context captures across four levels, daylight and late shadows. The separate mapped-water fixture keeps the open moat visible and the shore-adjusted derivative removes spikes around the battery. The original field was also rendered independently.

geographicReview.notes: Used the 29-corner native fortress polygon, separate bridge and bridge centerline and native retaining edges. Retained the unmasked 256 m source field for comparison. The supplemental water review applies a documented coastal adjustment in the source frame. Absolute river and foundation grades are approximate.

fidelityReview.scope: Standing Castillo de San Felipe de Lara at Río Dulce following the 1955 reconstruction and later conservation, including the full castle shell, river bastion, terraced court, roofed lookouts, retaining edges and landward entry bridge.
fidelityReview.notes: The cleared riverside oblique verifies the low gray rubble curtain, raised roofed features, and staggered stonework. The excavation report documents the semicircular battery, two mostly square towers and the three-level fort with a moat crossing. Other exact wall heights, roof slopes, internal court divisions and the fixed leaf and fittings are reconstructed estimates.

imageryReview.notes: Used the exact Qualla waterside photograph by sjc196. Its 2008 own-work upload and public-domain grant are recorded in the first Wikimedia migration revision, and the sole native photograph matches Qualla byte for byte. The geometry uses only architectural observations.

validation.sharedCaptureScope: The standing rebuilt fortress at the entrance to Lake Izabal, including its tower and battery volumes, mapped bridge and retaining edges.

limitations: Represents the standing reconstruction with the mapped castle, approach bridge and waterfront stone edge. The river parapet height is documented. Internal subdivisions, other wall heights, turret roof pitches and precise arch and crenel positions are estimates.
The static drawbridge leaf, fittings and courtyard transitions represent visible architectural form. Rooms and moving machinery are outside exterior scope.

The original public DEM is preserved. The waterfront review uses a separate mapped water plane and a coastally adjusted derivative of the original terrain to approximate shoreline grade. Runtime retains the mapped terrain and water. Vertical registration remains approximate.
